<details><summary>Is this AI tools training?</summary><p>Participants practise framing, evaluating and justifying decisions, and design where people and machines may act. Tool use supports those activities; the sessions are not a tour of AI features.</p></details>
<details><summary>Do participants need technical knowledge?</summary><p>No coding knowledge is required. We agree the starting point in advance, including participants’ experience with AI.</p></details>
<details><summary>Is it tied to ChatGPT or a particular platform?</summary><p>The framework is platform-independent. Tool choices for exercises are agreed with your organisation.</p></details>
<details><summary>Can we use our own workflows?</summary><p>Yes. We can work with a relevant workflow or document, subject to agreed confidentiality and tool-use boundaries. An anonymised or synthetic example is an alternative.</p></details>
<details><summary>Is it suitable for leadership teams?</summary><p>The briefing helps leaders separate production from judgment and identify capabilities at risk of erosion. A workflow lab can examine how their team reviews work, delegates decisions and responds to failure.</p></details>
<details><summary>Can workshops be delivered virtually?</summary><p>Discuss the proposed format, group size and collaboration needs with us. Delivery arrangements are agreed before an engagement is confirmed.</p></details>
<details><summary>How is confidentiality handled?</summary><p>We agree what material can be used, which platforms are permitted and what must be anonymised or excluded. Do not send confidential documents with an initial enquiry.</p></details>
<details><summary>Can it fit our existing AI policies?</summary><p>Yes. Existing policies and governance requirements become constraints for the exercises and workflow design. Specific arrangements are agreed during scoping.</p></details>
